title_en: The Ras (round-dance hymn) of the Great Ganapati
translation:
Heading: Here begins the Ras (round-dance hymn) of the great Ganapati ||1||

1. Great Ganapati, the god of the mighty belly, the lord who removes obstacles, the brother [of Kartikeya] - at his feet I make my obeisance. Hari, Hari.

2. She holds the veena and the book in her hands; mounted on the swan she places her gift in the poet's hand; she destroys the very root of dull-wittedness. Hari, Hari.

3. Bowing my head at the feet of the goddess Sarasvati, by whose grace the gift of poetry is won - Lord, I shall sing the praises of Govind. Hari, Hari.

4. He who created all beings, moving and unmoving; who pervades water, land, earth and every world; and who kindled the blaze of delusion (moh). Hari, Hari.

5. He watches over the soul that dwells within the body; when it strays onto the wrong road, He turns it back. Serving Him puts an end to worldly bondage (sansar). Hari, Hari.

6. In an instant He fashions many universes and destroys them; the all-pervading One Himself dwells in the three worlds; and laughing, He makes sport of it all. Hari, Hari.

7. He is close at hand, yet the soul does not long for Him; drunk on its own deeds (karma) it will not worship Him; and death seizes it from within. Hari, Hari.

8. He makes the man without devotion perform deeds, and to reap those deeds He makes him take a body. But what deeds bind His servant? Hari, Hari.

9. In every pore of Him many universes are contained; Brahma and the other gods, Sanaka and the other sages, run in search - yet they do not reach His limit. Hari, Hari.

10. That Lord is contained alike in the body and in the universe; sages, gods, demons and men have not fathomed Him; He alone knows Himself. Hari, Hari.

11. Know that to serve Hari is unshakable happiness. Why fix your mind on this perishing thing? Nectar is being poured out for you - do not spill it. Hari, Hari.

12. Put away the craving for what pleases the senses; in heart, word and deed contemplate Vishnu; then you will pass beyond the net of worldly existence. Hari, Hari.

13. In the form of the Fish (Matsya) He slew Shankhasur; in his goodness He carried [his own] across the ocean of existence; He drove unrighteousness out of the worlds. Hari, Hari.

14. In the form of the Tortoise (Kurma) He bore up Mount Mandar; gods and demons alike plunged in and laboured; and the Ocean of Milk was churned. Hari, Hari.

15. At the time of dissolution, when the earth lay sunk in the waters, the primordial Boar (Varah) lifted her upon the tip of his tusk - when the destruction of the worlds was at hand. Hari, Hari.

16. Hiranyakashipu was renowned through the three worlds; in battle he defeated the hosts and Indra, lord of the gods; his undoing came through a sage's curse. Hari, Hari.

17. For the sake of his son and to fulfil his longing, in the form of Narsinh (the Man-Lion) He tore him open with His claws and slew the demon king. Hari, Hari.

18. For Indra's sake He undid the strength of Bali's sacrifice; as Vaman He made Bali dwell in the netherworld; and the worlds dwelt without fear. Hari, Hari.

19. As Parashuram He broke the lords of the kshatriyas; He requited the offence done to the great sage; and He established the brahmin folk. Hari, Hari.

20. He took birth as an avatar in the royal line of Raghu; the wish in the heart of Indra was fulfilled; and He showed His grace to the gods. Hari, Hari.

21. Dasharath was filled with supreme joy; the sorrow and grief of childlessness was taken away; four sons became the lamps of his line. Hari, Hari.

22. His is the name whose recitation the shruti (revealed scripture) prescribes, at the mere remembrance of which heaps of sin are destroyed - so the Vedas and the Puranas declare. Hari, Hari.

23. There Ramchandra grew day by day; as if in play the Lord accomplished every task; and He upheld his own dharma. Hari, Hari.

24. In his play he guarded the great sage's sacrifice; Hari removed the torment caused by the demons; and he redeemed the body of Ahalya. Hari, Hari.

25. In play he broke the bow of Tripurari (Shiva); at the sound of it the three worlds began to tremble; he broke it as easy sport. Hari, Hari.

26. In the three worlds there was unceasing festival; the bridegroom of Sita, the most beautiful in all three worlds; gods and men rejoiced in their hearts. Hari, Hari.

27. The four brothers, being married, set out; Parashuram's heart was pierced with rage; the mountains and crags shook. Hari, Hari.

28. Parashuram recognized him as the supreme Lord; when he strung the bow, conviction came; he knew him for the highest of the gods. Hari, Hari.

29. The Lord of play came to Ayodhya; the beautiful bridegroom was welcomed with showers of pearls; he was lovely to look upon as the moon. Hari, Hari.

30. Seeing the king bound by his word to the mother, he set aside the kingdom of Ayodhya and took on the garb of a forest exile. Hari, Hari.

31. With Lakshman and Sita, the eternal Lord went to the forest of Mount Chitrakut; [meanwhile] his father departed to the world of the gods. Hari, Hari.

32. Bharat was fetched from his mother's family; they offered him the robes and the coronation; [instead] he came to where Shri Ram was. Hari, Hari.

33. "Be gracious, Lord, and come back to the city; master, take up your father's kingdom" - so Bharat spoke with the deepest humility. Hari, Hari.

34. Ramchandra gave him counsel; Bharat set the sandals (paduka) upon the throne; and so he was given a rule he was not to enjoy himself. Hari, Hari.

35. The Lord moved on from Chitrakut; the master of divine play reached the southern country; and there he received the honour of many sages. Hari, Hari.

36. The jar-born sage [Agastya] gave him his instruction; Ramchandra went on to the Panchavati forest, holding joy in his heart. Hari, Hari.

37. A night-roaming demoness came, tormented with lust; Lakshman dealt with Shurpanakha and cut off her ears and nose. Hari, Hari.

38. Fourteen thousand demons were hunted down in battle; grieving at that, the city of Lanka turned hostile; and Marich carried out his deed [of the golden deer]. Hari, Hari.

39. He cut down the lord of the monkeys [Vali]; in his place he installed Sugriv; and gave him an unshakable kingdom. Hari, Hari.

40. On Mount Malyavan, Sugriv sustained them; the monkey [Hanuman] burned the city of Lanka and came back; and the army of monkeys gathered. Hari, Hari.

41. Ramchandra's host reached the ocean; there the monkey Nal built the bridge; and in a moment they crossed to the other side. Hari, Hari.

42. The night-rangers fell upon the battlefield; Ravan was slain together with his kin; the arrow severed all ten of his heads. Hari, Hari.

43. Joy could not be contained in all the worlds; Ramchandra took Sita and entered the city of Ayodhya. Hari, Hari.

44. In the form of Krishna he was born in Gokul; he held up Mount Govardhan on his hand; the gopis chose Govind [as their beloved]. Hari, Hari.

45. A crown of peacock feathers graces his head; by his own maya the Lord graces the three worlds; a garland of gunja berries adorns him. Hari, Hari.

46. Flute in hand, he sounds the horn; surrounded by the cowherds he goes along; in him the Vedas find the Parabrahman (the supreme reality). Hari, Hari.

47. Hari delights in every form and every hue; in Vrindavan he dances among the gopis; and yet he is the true brahmachari (the pure celibate). Hari, Hari.

48. Unfathomable, beyond all possibility, thus was he seen; he entered Gokul in the play of a child; he is the one upon whom Dhruv and Shuk sat in meditation. Hari, Hari.

49. The infinite one stayed eleven years [in Gokul]; then Akrur came with the summons; Govind, the twenty-sixth [beyond the twenty-five principles]. Hari, Hari.

50. The dark one is the Parabrahman, having no [mortal] body; yet for the sake of curds the charming one presses his demand; he is never in want of anything. Hari, Hari.

51. In the form of Buddha, Hari taught meditation and reflection; in the form of Kalanki he destroys the barbarians; and he takes care of his own people. Hari, Hari.

52. Set the dark-hued Hari within your heart; make your play in the name of Hari, lord of the three worlds; bathe in supreme bliss. Hari, Hari.

53. For the fruit of devotion (bhakti) to Vishnu and of liberation, Dhanraj himself composed this ras; do your work in the name of Hari. Hari, Hari.

Colophon: Thus the Ras of the great Ganapati is complete ||1||
